approach: Add a records-derived hold. In scope_guard.rs, `RequestRecord` gets an `unlanded` flag (set in `request_records` for a job that is Blocked, or Dispatched with a passing verification, and has no finished attempt). New `non_landed_attempts` counts a line's Rejected and Failed attempts through `group_lines`/`line_attempts`, plus its `unlanded` requests. It ignores Environment attempts and counts nothing on a line with an Accepted attempt. New `hold_reason(requests, job_id)` returns a reason when that count is 2 or more. In drain.rs a new default method `Steps::awaiting(jobs)` (real impl: `request_records` + `hold_reason`) is asked in `Drain::prepare` (merged into the paused/held map, so a held item is not read, planned or run and `athena plan` lists it as held) and at the top of each `Drain::attempts` iteration after the pause check (new `ItemEnd::Awaiting(reason)`, passed over with the reason). Nothing is written, so no record or data file changes and the hold is recomputed from committed records on every drain run. Signals T1 to T5 are untouched because `unlanded` never enters `attempts`.

decisions.choice: Count a line's non-landed attempts with a new `scope_guard::non_landed_attempts` built on `group_lines` and `line_attempts`, and expose `hold_reason` over `&[RequestRecord]` so the drain tests can feed real `RequestRecord` values.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for the grouping the scope guard uses and forbids a second line-grouping function. A pure function over `RequestRecord` is testable without git. `Athena::line_pause`, `line_flag` and `live_marks` already group the same way.

rejected.option: Count attempts inside drain.rs from its own job list
rejected.why: The drain's `jobs` list is per run, so it would not see earlier runs. It would also be a second grouping.

rejected.option: Write a pause or flag file for the held line
rejected.why: Pause files lift only by deleting a file and feed `athena status` and T-signal logic. That is the follow-up line-field and status work, and a pause would change what `line_pause` reports.

decisions.choice: Represent a verified-but-not-landed job (Blocked, or Dispatched with a passing verification, no finished attempt) as a new bool `RequestRecord.unlanded`, not as an `AttemptRecord` or a new `Verdict` variant.
decisions.reason: `counted()` treats every verdict except Environment as an attempt for T1, T2 and T5, and T3 sums cost over all attempts, so a new variant or an extra attempt would change T1 to T5 behavior, which is out of scope. `verdict_of` already returns None for Blocked and Dispatched jobs. Stale and gate-refused jobs are already Failed attempts, so only Blocked and open jobs need the flag. `RequestRecord` is built in only two places, both in scope_guard.rs.

rejected.why: Changes `counted`, `t1_retries`, `t3_basis` and `rejections` results; would need threshold review.

rejected.option: Change `verdict_of` so Blocked and open jobs become Failed
rejected.why: Same signal change, and it would turn a job awaiting `go` into a failure for status and Hestia.

decisions.choice: Ask the hold in two places: `prepare` (beside `paused`, before any read) and the top of the `attempts` loop (after the pause check, before each read or run). Do not add it after the last failed attempt.
decisions.reason: The top-of-loop check is the one that stops the retry: with one earlier failure, one new failure makes two, and the second attempt is not made. It also stops a second drain run, because the item stays queued after a double failure (test at tests/drain.rs:1066). The `prepare` check avoids paying a planning read for an unread 'try again on' request on a held line. After a fresh item's two attempts the existing Paused, Flagged and Failed ends keep their text, so existing tests are unchanged.

rejected.why: An unread 'try again on' request on a held line would still be read by the planning pass and cost a reader run.
The line count changes during a run, so the second attempt of an item would not be stopped.

decisions.choice: Precedence: a paused line is reported as paused first; the hold is asked only for jobs that are not paused. Reuse the `pause_held` map and the `Refusal::held` path for held items, with the dependents' reason saying 'its line is awaiting diagnosis' when the item they wait on was held by this rule.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert the paused text exactly ('depends on a, which is held back: its line is paused'). Reusing the map reuses pass_over_paused, the first_paused filtering and the `athena plan` held listing.

rejected.option: A second map and a second passed-over printer
rejected.why: Duplicates the held plumbing and risks double lines.

decisions.choice: Environment stops are never counted, and a line with an Accepted attempt is never held.
decisions.reason: This follows `counted()` and `done()` in scope_guard.rs (lines 222 to 233) and the request. Environment stops are not the work's fault, and an accepted line is finished.

rejected.why: Would hold lines for a full disk or an expired login.

decisions.choice: The reason text says 'awaiting diagnosis' and names the line, the counts and that the drain will not retry it. It never claims a diagnosis job exists, and never contains the word 'paused'.
decisions.reason: The request names the state; the diagnosis role is a follow-up. A real-steps test at tests/drain.rs:5628 asserts no plan refusal contains 'paused' for a flagged line.

rejected.why: Would tell the operator to delete a pause file that does not exist.

Add `HOLD_ATTEMPTS = 2`, `non_landed_attempts(requests, line)` and `hold_reason(requests, job_id)`. Update the `req()` test helper and add unit tests under `scope_guard::hold…`. T1 to T5 constants and functions are untouched.

Add default `Steps::awaiting`; `RealSteps::awaiting` over `request_records` and `hold_reason`; merge held items into `prepare`'s paused map with wording for dependents; check at the top of `Drain::attempts`; `ItemEnd::Awaiting(String)` and its `finish` arm (pass_over); module-doc bullet.
Stub gains `records` and `track_runs` and implements `awaiting` by calling production `hold_reason`; add the `awaiting_diagnosis_*` stub tests and one RealSteps test.
One Unreleased/Added bullet describing only the hold.

steps: scope_guard.rs: add `pub unlanded: bool` to `RequestRecord` with a doc comment (verified but not landed: blocked, or open with a passing verification, and no finished attempt; never in `attempts`, so T1 to T5 do not see it). In `request_records`, set it from a private `verified_unlanded(job: &JobRecords)`: `job.job.is_some()` and either `state() == JobState::Blocked` or `Dispatched` with `verification.final_verdict == athena_data::records::Verdict::Pass`, and only when `attempts` is empty. Update the `req()` test helper (line 1790).

scope_guard.rs: add `pub const HOLD_ATTEMPTS: usize = 2;`, `pub fn non_landed_attempts(requests, line) -> usize` (0 if `done(&line_attempts(..))`, else the Rejected and Failed attempts from `line_attempts` plus the `unlanded` requests of `line`), and `pub fn hold_reason(requests, job_id) -> Option<String>` (find the job's index, find its line with `group_lines`, return the reason text naming the first request id of the line, the counts and 'awaiting diagnosis' when the count reaches `HOLD_ATTEMPTS`). Add unit tests: counts with Environment, with Accepted, with unlanded; `hold_reason` None for an unknown job; derivation of `unlanded` from the rig's records (Blocked, open with Pass, open without verification); `evaluate_before_attempt` equal with and without unlanded requests.

drain.rs: add `fn awaiting(&self, _jobs: &[String]) -> Vec<(String, String)> { Vec::new() }` to `Steps` beside `flagged`, with a doc comment. Add `RealSteps::awaiting`: load records (none held when they cannot be loaded, as `paused` does), build `request_records` once, and map each job through `scope_guard::hold_reason`.

drain.rs: in `prepare`, after `paused` is computed, ask `awaiting` for the ids not already paused and add them to `paused` (the held map). In the dependents loop, word the reason as 'its line is awaiting diagnosis' when the item depended on is a hold item and keep 'its line is paused' otherwise.

drain.rs: add `ItemEnd::Awaiting(String)` with a doc comment. In `Drain::attempts`, right after the `paused_reason` check, call a new `awaiting_reason(item)` (same shape as `paused_reason`) and return `ItemEnd::Awaiting(reason)`. In `finish`, handle it like `Paused` and `Flagged` (`pass_over`). Update the module docs with a bullet: a line with two non-landed attempts is held and not retried.

tests/drain.rs: extend `Stub` with `records: RefCell<Vec<RequestRecord>>` and `track_runs: bool` and implement `awaiting` by calling `athena_core::scope_guard::hold_reason` over a clone of the records. In `run()`, when `track_runs`, update the record whose id is the job (or push one, with `retry_of` set by stripping the `-retry` suffix) with the attempt for the outcome: Rejected, Failed, Accepted, or `unlanded` when the job is in `unlandable`. Add the tests `awaiting_diagnosis_*` for: two earlier failures held and a second drain run held, plus `drain::plan` listing it; an earlier failure then a new failure so the second attempt is not made; a collision case (Failed plus unlanded, and unlanded plus unlanded); one failure retried as today; Environment attempts not counted. Add one RealSteps test: `rejected_twice(rejecting_verdict(), rejecting_second_criterion())`, queue `try again on <job>`, run `drain::drain` twice, and assert `fx.head()` is unchanged and the passed-over line contains 'awaiting diagnosis'.

CHANGELOG.md: insert one bullet at the end of `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` (before `### Changed` at line 423) stating only that the drain holds a line after two attempts that did not land and does not retry it, with the cause (a twice-failed line was queued and retried again, paying for each attempt).
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any existing test that fails only because its line now reaches two non-landed attempts.

risks.risk: An existing real-steps or lifecycle test has a line that already reaches two non-landed attempts and then expects a retry, so it now fails.
risks.mitigation: I read the real-steps drain tests that retry (tests/drain.rs 3100, 5121 to 5265). Those use environment stops or interrupted jobs, which are not counted, or fresh items. The producer runs the full `cargo test --locked` and updates only a test whose expectation is the retry itself.

risks.risk: A job that is Dispatched with a passing verification while its landing is in progress is counted as unlanded and causes a false hold.
risks.mitigation: The check runs only when an item has no passed job pending (`passed.is_none()`), and in `prepare` before work starts. The count needs a second non-landed attempt on the same line to hold. The Host question above records what was not traced.

risks.risk: A held line has no release: it stays held until it lands or the request is rephrased.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated scope; the reason text names the line and says the drain will not retry it. The release command is a follow-up. Nothing is written, so no cleanup is owed.

risks.risk: Adding a field to the public `RequestRecord` breaks other struct literals.
risks.mitigation: Searched all crates: literals exist only at scope_guard.rs:658 and in the `req()` helper at line 1790; status.rs and display.rs do not use it.

risks.risk: A hold at two attempts overlaps with the T1 flag at three and the T4 pause at two same-criterion rejections, so operators see two reasons.
risks.mitigation: A pause is reported first, and the hold is asked only for jobs that are not paused. A line held by this rule shows 'awaiting diagnosis', never 'paused'.

open_questions: User: There is no command to release a held line in this job (release is a named follow-up). Is it acceptable that the operator escapes a hold only by asking in new words, which starts a new line, until that follow-up exists?

Host: Is a job that is Dispatched with a passing verification ever running live (registered in the process registry) at a moment when another worker asks about its line? The code counts it as unlanded; it appears to occur only for an open pull request or an interrupted job, but the registry timing was not traced.
